notes: This file is the ONLY source of model ids for the Foundry runtime. Any id not listed here is rejected (tests/model-policy.test.mjs).

Classes are capability/cost tiers. For open-weight models they follow ROADMAP §2.3 parameter bands; hosted Anthropic models have no public parameter count, so they are placed by price tier and must be justified by measurement (research/*/REPORT.md).
No silent fallback: the runtime never substitutes a model. Escalation moves up the class order only through logged events (rules E1-E7).

Costs: hosted calls record the provider-reported list-price USD (claude CLI total_cost_usd, costBasis=list). Local CPU calls record API cost 0 plus an imputed compute cost = wall seconds x imputedComputeUsdPerHour/3600.

2026-10-07: Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) added as the first class-M model (owner notice: Anthropic replaced Haiku 4.5 with Haiku 5.5). Class M resolves to it; Haiku 4.5 stays listed by id for earlier pilots and tests only. Local S-class models are parked (owner decision 2026-10-07) but stay listed.

2026-10-08: claude-cli.childEnv sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 and FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1 for every claude -p child (research/review-20261007/04-efficiency-rust.md change 1; re-measured in research/review-20261007/cli-flags-20261008/). Closed list of transport/telemetry/cache-pricing variables, validated in src/models/policy.mjs; each journal request records the closed-list variables the child saw (providerRequest.env). Excluded from replay keys because neither changes the decoding; the first does shorten the prompt the CLI builds (about 165 tokens; the CLI's telemetry plugin is not loaded), as a CLI version change can. The flags lower the reported cost per call, so cost per success before and after 2026-10-08 is not comparable (synthesis rule R3). A value is "1" (set) or null (removed from the child); "0" is refused because the CLI reads CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=0 as set (zero-probe.json). Version 2026-10-08.2 corrects this note only; the measurements in that directory ran under 2026-10-08.1.

2026-10-09: owner direction, Jev replaces Kev for the judge program; billed to the owner's TypeSafe account. Jev (TypeSafe's hosted System One judgment model) is listed under judgmentModels on the systemone-http provider typesafe-systemone: typed questions in, a probability per option out. It is not a generative model: ModelPort and class resolution read models[] only, and validatePolicy refuses a models[] entry on a systemone-http provider. The provider names its credential variable (credentialEnv), never a value; the owner maps his own key into that variable per command. jev-latest is a moving alias, so every judgment records the version the response names (its model field); TypeSafe documents no /v1/models.

2026-10-15 (P0 policy batch: research/architecture-20261014/MEMORY-ROUTING-RECURSION.md §2 changes 1 and 6, §5 row 1; recorded as deviation D6 in research/need-router-20261014/PREREG-NEED-V1.md §13). (1) Jev is pinned: the judgment model id is the served version jev-1.13.0, not the moving alias jev-latest (which serves jev-1.13.0 today; jev-1.14.0 shipped on 2026-10-14 behind jev-preview). Callers request the pinned id; a deliberate re-read on another version names that id explicitly (score-served.mjs and jev-need.mjs --jev-model), and the id must be listed here. Every judgment still records the version its response names. (2) inputBudgetTokensByClass M, L and F are 100000 (were 8000, 16000, 32000). The 8000 class-M budget dates from class M meaning a 7-14B open model; M1 (research/need-router-20261014/runs/m1) measured one Haiku 5.5 call solving 45-64K-token tasks. 100000 is the Haiku price-tier boundary in its price source; L and F get the same budget so an escalation never lands in a smaller one. S stays 4000 (parked). (3) defaultsByRole is removed: no code read it, and wiring a role-based automatic assignment is on the design's do-not-build list (§4).

2026-10-15.2 (same deviation D6, before the NL0 stamp): jev-1.14.0 is listed beside the pinned jev-1.13.0 so the planned J0 re-read can name it explicitly; the default pinned id is unchanged (the first judgment entry).

2026-10-21.1 (owner decision 2026-10-21, research/mercury-20261021/PROVISIONING.md): Inception's Mercury models are added as a second cheap executor beside Haiku 5.5. Provider inception has the new kind openai-chat-https (a remote OpenAI-compatible chat.completions endpoint, https only; validated in src/models/policy.mjs: no credential field, no key-like value, no field outside a closed list). The key is named by credentialEnv (INCEPTION_API_KEY), read only by src/executors/openai-chat.mjs at call time from the host environment, never passed into the executor sandbox, never stored, logged or committed. The models are listed under executorModels, apart from models[], as judgmentModels are: ModelPort has no provider for this kind, so class resolution and escalation never route a typed node to one; they serve only executor sessions (the tool-using loop of src/executors/openai-chat.mjs, tools run in the claude-code executor sandbox). Class M is the tier of record: hosted models without a public parameter count are placed by price tier (notes above), S is the parked local <=4B band with a 4,000-token input budget, and Mercury's listed prices put mercury-2.5 beside Haiku (M); mercury-3 is listed free today. The placement must be justified by measurement like any other. Every entry above is unchanged.

typesafe-systemone.docs: https://docs.typesafe.ai/api.md (checked 2026-10-09): POST /v1/systemone {model, state, questions}; answers carry the probabilities, the response carries model and usage {input_tokens, output_tokens}; errors 401 auth, 422 validation, 429 rate limit (exponential backoff), 529 overloaded (retry).
knownGaps: no documented /v1/models: the served version is read from each response's model field
pricing and rate limits are undocumented: record usage tokens per request

inception.auth: Authorization: Bearer <value of the environment variable named in credentialEnv>, read at call time by src/executors/openai-chat.mjs on the host (never inside the executor sandbox). The owner keeps the key outside the repository and loads it per command (research/mercury-20261021/PROVISIONING.md); no key is read from a file by code, stored, logged or committed.
inception.docs: GET https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1/models (public, read 2026-10-21): endpoint chat.completions only (OpenAI-compatible); mercury-3, mercury-2.5 and mercury-2 list the features tools, json_mode and structured_outputs and the sampling parameters temperature and stop. reasoning_effort is accepted but showed no consistent effect (PROVISIONING.md smoke tests); usage reports reasoning tokens.
knownGaps: no documented default temperature: none is set here, so the provider default applies and every transcript records that none was sent
reasoning_effort is accepted without a measured effect; the executor forwards low, medium or high when a caller asks and refuses other levels
rate limits and the free allowance are not published in the models listing: the executor maps HTTP 429 to MODEL_RATE_LIMIT after bounded retries
